title: H. G. Wells: The War of the Worlds — Ep 21/27 — "The Death of the Curate"
description:
On the sixth day the narrator wrestles a bottle from the curate in the pantry doorway until it bursts on the bricks. He bars the curate from the food and splits what remains into ten piles, rationed for ten days.

A night and a day they sit facing each other across the scullery, the curate weeping with hunger while the narrator fights off sleep. For two days he beats, coaxes and bribes him with wine, but neither force nor kindness reaches a man gone mad.

By the eighth day the curate is on his knees, crying his witness to God despite every hiss to be still, and bolts for the kitchen door. The narrator catches him and strikes him down with the butt of the meat chopper — and the wall collapses into light.

A handling-machine slides into the gap, its tentacle dragging the curate toward the pit. The narrator flees to the coal cellar and buries himself under coal; a groping tentacle finds his boot heel and takes only a lump of coal. He lies buried through the tenth day, and dares not stir until the eleventh.

Chapter IV of Book Two of H. G. Wells's The War of the Worlds (1898), "The Death of the Curate", in the public domain.

— The Keeper's Lantern —
Every episode is one whole chapter, in order, from the first page to the last.
